subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Guessing vocabulary from context (Activity 3) / Listening for specific information; grouping words (Top Tip)
outcomes: Use strategies for dealing with new words
Guess the meaning of words from context
Listen for specific information and group words into lexical fields

tf.s: Guessing from context means using the words around an unknown word.
tf.why: Yes, the words before and after give clues.

tf.s: Looking up a word in a dictionary is one strategy for new words.
tf.why: Correct, it is useful when the word is important.

tf.s: Guessing from context wastes time and stops you reading.
tf.why: It saves time and keeps you reading.
Right, the listening says he is in Grade 12.
He wants to study airport management.

tf.s: Majid's father prefers London to Chichester.
tf.why: He prefers Chichester so Majid will speak English with local people.

tf.s: Chichester has a direct rail link to London.
tf.why: Yes, this is one of its advantages.

tf.s: A lexical field is a group of words with associated meanings.
tf.why: Correct, like campus, lecturer, degree and tutor.

tf.s: Grouping words by topic makes vocabulary harder to remember.
tf.why: Grouping helps you remember words by topic.

tf.s: A dictionary is better when the word is essential and the context gives few clues.
tf.why: Yes, then guessing is not enough.

boxes.q: What is one strategy for a new word?
What helps you guess a meaning?
o: the words before and after it

boxes.q: What does Majid want to study?
boxes.why: He is interested in airport management.

boxes.q: Which city does Majid's father prefer?
Why does his father prefer Chichester?
o: Majid will speak English with locals
boxes.why: In London he might speak Arabic with friends.

boxes.q: Where would Majid live in Chichester?
boxes.why: A host family helps his English.

boxes.q: What field do campus, lecturer, degree and tutor belong to?

o: a group of words on one topic

boxes.q: Where can you record new words?
boxes.why: A notebook helps you review words.

hunt.q: City the father does not choose

mcq.q: Which are strategies for dealing with new words?
o: ignore it, use a dictionary or guess from context
ask the teacher to remove it
mcq.why: These are the strategies the class listed.

mcq.q: What advantages of Chichester does Majid's father give?
o: a small city near the sea with a direct rail link to London
it is the biggest city in the world
mcq.why: These make Chichester a good choice.

mcq.q: Which word belongs to the lexical field 'university life'?
mcq.why: Lecture is part of university life.

mcq.q: What should you do before listening to the father–son dialogue?
mcq.why: Reading first tells you what to listen for.

mcq.q: 'The exhausted runner sat down after the long race.' What does 'exhausted' mean?
mcq.why: After a long race, the runner would be very tired.

mcq.q: Which word does NOT belong with campus, lecturer and degree?
mcq.why: Speed limit belongs to road safety.

mcq.q: You meet a new word, and the sentence still makes sense without it. What is the best strategy?
o: keep reading and guess from context
stop and look up every word

mcq.q: Why does Majid's father think Chichester is better than London for him?
o: he will use English with local people instead of Arabic with friends
mcq.why: Speaking English daily improves his language.

mcq.q: When is a dictionary better than guessing from context?
o: when the word is essential and the context gives few clues
mcq.why: Use a dictionary when guessing cannot work.

mcq.q: Why is grouping words into lexical fields helpful?
o: it helps you remember vocabulary by topic
mcq.why: Linked words are easier to remember together.
